findings.class: counter blind spot vs the round's own deliverable
findings.claim: At the fixed pole the counter reports grammar 9/9, but `repeat-control --selftest` prints `REPEAT_CONTROL: setup_error` on stdout under an unusable TMPDIR. The round's integration item 1 says 'stdout carries no setup error'; the counter cannot see it because its stdout leg is two literal tokens (`RuntimeError`, `Traceback`), not 'no setup-error token'.
findings.output: rc=2; stdout: REPEAT_CONTROL: setup_error; stderr: repeat-control: could-not-evaluate: ...

findings.class: frozen before-receipt disagrees with a re-run of the frozen counter
findings.claim: `.ufo/evidence/round-55/before/c2.stdout` as committed at 133b2ce prints `total=21` with the arm vector `grammar=6/9 lazy=5/5 empty=13/13 usable=13/13 tmp_mkdirs=0 docs=0/7 note=0/9 skill=0/1`. The counter's own arithmetic on that vector is 3+7+9+1=20, and an independent re-run at the same rev prints `total=20`. All 42 EXPLAIN lines are byte-identical between the two files; only the total differs. Reported, not fixed (frozen).

findings.class: the usable arm can flake under host load
findings.claim: In a 10-way concurrent batch on the pre-amendment-8 bytes (usable-arm code unchanged), `registry-check --selftest` returned rc 1 on the usable arm in 3 of 9 fixed-tree cells, turning a PASS into `total=1 C2_R55_PASS=false`; a serial re-run of the same three cells gave total=0, and the mode standalone passed 5/5. A deciding run executed while other agents run counters can therefore report a false FAIL.

findings.class: base conflates three grammar failure modes
findings.claim: At base both failing modes print the class on stdout and carry `RuntimeError`, so the grammar arm fails them for the stream, the shape and the token at once. Mutants that relax any single leg (m2, m3, m9) still fail base, so base cannot tell the counter's legs apart; only a tree that violates one leg at a time can.
findings.receipt: receipts/verdicts/m2-base2.stdout, m3-base2.stdout, m9-base2.stdout (all identical to P-base2)

findings.class: the pre-registered CTL_BREAK_c2 cannot apply to this round's tree
findings.claim: controls.sh:134 rewrites `emit_err(f"repeat-control: could-not-evaluate: {exc}")`, which occurs 0 times at the base rev, at 133b2ce and in the worktree; the landed tool emits `emit_err(f"repeat-control: could-not-evaluate: {message}")` (tools/repeat-control.py:233). Reproduced in a scratch clone at 133b2ce: the `assert src.count(old) == 1` aborts, the clone stays clean, `gitcommit` exits 1 (no --allow-empty), and `|| exit 2` (controls.sh:136) ends phase b before the control is scored - so controls-b.stdout cannot carry `CONTROLS_B: n/n as pre-registered` and deciding-run.sh:56-57 refuses the deciding run. Secondary: even if the anchor matched, that control trips the line-shape and raw-type legs together and exercises neither the exit class (m1) nor the stderr-only leg (m3); no pre-registered control violates the lazy arm (m5), the empty arm (m6) or the /tmp census (m10).

findings.class: the docs arm counts cells, it does not identify them
findings.claim: `docs` is `sum(...)` over the rows that carry a `scratch_root` cell AND mention one of the seven tool paths, guarded only by `len(cells) != 7` (measure.py:245-249). A tree whose seven cells belong to the wrong modes (or to a ninth allocating mode) still scores 7/7 as long as the marker text is present. Not scored as a mutant (no tree was built for it); recorded as the arm's known limit.
